Become better at detect hidden." Click the button beside Remove Trap in your skills window and choose a container within 2 tiles. If it has no trap you are told "That doesn't appear to be trapped.", so the skill is also a safe way to check.

Your chance is how far your skill is above the trap's strength, out of 30: nothing at the trap's strength, certain 30 points above it. On success you are told "You successfully render the trap harmless." A failure is harmless too: "You fail to disarm the trap...but you don't set it off." Afterwards no skill can be used for 10 seconds.
To check a container without touching it, point Detecting Hidden at it: "[trapped]" shows over it if it has a trap and your roll works.
# Traps

The strength of a trap decides how hard it is to disarm:
A chest from a treasure map: 25 times its level, so 25 to 125.
A chest that refills itself: 10 to 30 times its level (1 to 3), new each time it refills.
A trap a tinker sets: 9 times a tenth of the tinker's Tinkering, rounded down, so 27 at Tinkering 30 to 39, 54 at 60 to 69 and 90 at 100.
The Magic Trap spell (second circle Magery): 1.

A trap has a level: 1 to 3 on a chest that refills itself, 1 to 5 on a treasure chest, and a tenth of the tinker's Tinkering on a tinker's trap, so up to 10. An explosion burns for 10 to 30 times the level, a dart hits for 5 to 15 times the level, and a poison trap poisons at a strength that rises with the level, from Lesser at level 1 to Lethal at level 5. The Magic Trap spell does 1 damage. You are hurt only if you stand within 3 tiles (1 tile for the Magic Trap).
# Training it

You learn only from a trap whose strength is no higher than your skill and less than 30 below it, and no trap is weaker than 1. So Remove Trap cannot be learned from nothing: at skill 0 no trap can teach you. Begin with a lesson from a Tinker, the Tinkers' Guildmaster or the Thieves' Guildmaster in Britain, once your Lockpicking and Detecting Hidden are 50 each. It raises you to about 25 to 33, for 1 gold for each 0.1 point (see Training in the Welcome guide, [Welcome).

From there you need traps of the right strength. A trap set by a tinker (a character with the Tinkering skill) teaches from its strength to 30 above it:
Tinkering 30 to 39: 27 to 57
Tinkering 40 to 49: 36 to 66
Tinkering 50 to 59: 45 to 75
Tinkering 60 to 69: 54 to 84
Tinkering 70 to 79: 63 to 93
Tinkering 80 to 89: 72 to 102
Tinkering 90 to 99: 81 to 111
Tinkering 100: 90 to 120

So to reach 100 you need a tinker with Tinkering 80 or more. To set a trap a tinker double-clicks Tinker's Tools and chooses Traps: a dart trap (Tinkering 30 to 80, one iron ingot and one crossbow bolt), a poison trap (30 to 80, an iron ingot and a poison potion) or an explosion trap (55 to 105, an iron ingot and an explosion potion). Then point at an unlocked box or crate that has a key and is not locked down. The trap is live only while the box is locked, and it goes off on whoever picks the lock: lock the box with its key to arm it, and unlocking it with its key switches it off for the moment. Remove Trap can disarm it at any time.
# What you need

No tool. You need traps to practise on: a tinker friend (or your own Tinkering) and boxes that have keys. A tinker pays for each trap with an iron ingot (a blacksmith sells them for about 5 gold) plus a crossbow bolt (a provisioner, about 5 gold), a Lesser Poison Potion (an alchemist, about 15 gold) or a Lesser Explosion Potion (about 21 gold). The Magic Trap spell makes a trap of strength 1, which teaches only from 1 to 31.
# Good to know

A failed try never sets a trap off. The danger is opening or picking a trapped chest, so disarm first. A chest from a treasure map (level 1 or more) is always trapped with an explosion, so check it before you open it.
# What it is
Detecting Hidden finds what is hiding: hidden players and monsters, and the traps on containers. The better your skill, the wider your search.
# How to use it

Click the button beside Detecting Hidden in your skills window, then point at the ground up to 12 tiles away, or at yourself. (Pointing at another character searches nothing.) Everything hidden within a radius of one tenth of your skill, rounded down, of that spot is checked: up to 10 tiles at skill 100, and nothing below skill 10. If your roll fails, the radius is halved.

A hidden character is found when your skill, give or take 10, is at least their Hiding, give or take 10. They are told "You have been revealed!" It finds your friends and party members too. If nobody is found you are told "You can see nothing hidden there."
Point at a container instead and, if it is within that radius of you and your roll works, "[trapped]" shows over it when it has a trap.

Without the button you still get a free roll against a hidden player you are allowed to attack, whenever either of you moves within 4 tiles of the other (see the Hiding page). Party members and guild allies are skipped.
# Training it

Every search is a roll against your skill out of 100, and it teaches whether or not anyone is hiding, so you can train alone: point at yourself again and again. Every try below 10.0 teaches, even though the radius is nothing yet. Past that, the lower your chance, the more often a try teaches.
The Thieves' Guildmaster in Britain teaches Detecting Hidden for 1 gold per 0.1 point, up to a third of its own skill: about 25 to 33 (see Training in [Welcome).

A friend who hides and stays put lets you practise the real thing: stand a few tiles off, inside your search radius, and search. A searcher whose skill is 20 or more above your Hiding always finds you, and one more than 20 below never does. In between it is a roll.
The radius grows with your skill: 1 tile at skill 10, 5 tiles at 50, 10 tiles at 100.
# What you need
Nothing: no tool and no gold.
# Good to know
Inside a house you own or are a friend of, point at a spot in the house: the radius is 22 tiles and anyone hidden inside that house is found, however well they hide.
Remove Trap needs Detecting Hidden 50, so train it before that skill. Some monsters have it and look for hidden players in sight now and then.
# What it is
Begging asks a non-player for a little gold. It pays little and costs karma, which is your good or evil reputation, so it is mostly a way to train a skill.
# How to use it

Click the button beside Begging in your skills window and choose a person within 2 tiles. You bow, and after 2 seconds the person either gives you gold or does not. You are revealed if you were hidden. You can use the skill again 10 seconds after you used it.

It works only on non-players who look human, such as shopkeepers and townsfolk. From another player you are told "Perhaps just asking would work better." and from an animal or monster, "There is little chance of getting money from that!" You cannot beg while riding a mount: "They seem unwilling to give you any money."
# What you get

A person gives you a tenth of the gold in their pack, never more than 10 gold at once (up to 14 if you are famous, 1 more for each 2,500 fame). A person with less than 10 gold says "I have not enough money to give thee any!" Shopkeepers start with 100 to 200 gold, and what they give you comes out of their own packs. There is no limit per person, only the 10-second wait and the person's gold. Fame is how well known you are; killing monsters raises it.

Each gift costs you about 40 karma (more if your karma is high), until your karma reaches -3000. And while your karma is below zero, the person refuses you outright with a chance of at least 50 in 100, more the lower your karma is: "Thou dost not look trustworthy... no gold for thee today!" That refusal comes before your skill roll, so it teaches you nothing. Stealing and Snooping cost karma too. Killing evil monsters raises it again.
# Training it

Your chance is your Begging out of 100. At skill 0 you cannot succeed yet, but every try below 10.0 teaches. Past that, the lower your chance, the more often a try teaches. A person who has run dry still counts: your roll is made first, so it teaches you either way. Then move on to someone else.

Every gift lowers your karma, so it soon falls below zero. Keep it at zero or above while you train, or at least half your tries are wasted on refusals. When it has fallen, go and kill some evil monsters before you beg again.
# What you need
Nothing: no tool and no gold, only a person who has some, and good karma.
# Good to know

Begging reveals you. It is not a crime and no guard reacts to it. The gold is small, so do not count on it for a living: a shopkeeper with 150 gold gives 10 at a time at first, and less as the pack empties.
